anchor.quote: Let $N$ be the number of coefficients in the list
let $d$ be the number of axes
Let $q_1,\dots,q_d$ be the prime lengths of the axes
Let $e$ be a position in the list, running from $0$ to $N-1$.

gaps.quote: The map preserves [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) of length $N$
gaps.note: The page asserts that the map preserves cyclic convolution of length N but never states what the transformed convolution is on the axes (which product is carried to which). The source paper is credited with the proof, without a (cited) marker and without saying what it establishes, so the reader cannot check that the placement preserves convolution.

gaps.quote: It is implemented by [fast address interchange](address-interchange.md) steps.
gaps.note: The page claims the map is realised by fast address interchange steps but does not say which interchanges are used or how they produce the residue placement. The linked page explains interchange, not this construction.

gaps.term: controlled cyclic shifts as interchange steps
gaps.note: The page classes controlled cyclic shifts among the interchange steps without showing how a rotation by a control-set amount is built from interchanges of address fields.

gaps.quote: The radix-digit coefficient list is placed on distinct prime axes (cited).
gaps.note: This cited claim carries the setup of the whole page. The page does not say which result of the source is stated here, nor why the radix-digit list is the list being placed, so the reader cannot check that the map applies to it.
